newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Buoyant Ruggiero predicts 'something big' at WTO.
newsitem.headline: Buoyant Ruggiero predicts 'something big' at WTO.

text.p: Despite sleepless nights and three days of intense negotiations, a buoyant Renato Ruggiero on Wednesday predicted "something big" from the World Trade Organisation's week-long inaugural ministerial conference.

"I am very encouraged. The sense of achievement is very clear," he told Reuters as he emerged at the half-way stage of the gathering from the latest of several sessions aimed at finalising a declaration for the ministers to sign.

"The road is open to something important, something big," declared the WTO's director-general, whose horizon has been set on the Singapore meeting since he took up the post 18 months ago just after the body was launched.

"We are deep in negotiation, and I do not want to prejudice anything," he said. "But there have been some very interesting proposals to get over some of the differences. People are ready for compromise to reach agreement."

For Ruggiero, long a senior official of the European Union who as a young Italian diplomat in Moscow cut his negotiating teeth in endless sessions with intransigent Soviet bureaucrats, agreement on a meaningful declaration is vital.
And he is aware that he is still facing a major battle in Singapore before the conference wraps up on Friday.

"Near the end of the road there are always difficulties to be overcome," he told Reuters. Ministers at the gathering reflected political and public views in their own countries which they could not ignore.

Over the past three months, he and his closest aides at the WTO's Geneva headquarters have drafted and redrafted clauses and sub-clauses to try to include the concerns of all of the organisations's now 128 members.

The document is intended as a blueprint consolidating agreements already reached in the 1986-93 Uruguay Round of world trade talks -- in areas ranging from tariffs on industrial goods to services, farm produce and textiles.

But it will also set the course and the tone for discussions between now and the end of the century on topics not yet fully under the WTO purview such as basic telecommunications, financial and maritime services, and many others.

The big battle has been over whether to include a reference to core labour standards in the document and whether it should include provision for some discussion in the WTO on investment rules, competition policies and the way national authorities award contracts, or government procurement.
The bluff, sturdily built Ruggiero angered some developing country envoys back in Geneva for coming out openly last month in support of talks on the investment issue.
In Singapore, he has been rewarded as some of their ministers have softened their positions.
Diplomats from their countries' missions to WTO headquarters who have come to the conference have been impressed with the energy and stamina shown by Ruggiero, a 66-year-old grandfather.

An extrovert from Naples known for his love of classical music and an appetite for pasta, Ruggiero "loves being in the thick of it with the people who can really make decisions," said one, who asked not to be identified. "It gives him a totally different dimension."

A senior WTO aide with years of experience in his own country's bureaucracy voiced admiration for Ruggiero's commitment to the vision of free trade as the bringer of peace and prosperity to a troubled world.
"I've seen a lot of things and I've every reason to be a cynic," he said, "but this guy is for real. He believes totally in his cause."
